packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statisti: Internal hooks for counting feature usage inside the plugin. The original aggregates these counters locally and could upload them to the vendor; the replacement must keep the API callable but never upload usage statistics or contact the vendor (SPEC.md §1.8).
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur: The structure entity itself: reading and editing a structure's metadata (name, description, owner, permission rules, archive flag), looking structures up and checking access, creating, copying and deleting them, and listening for content changes.
Per-user favourite structures and the derived popularity count (how many users marked a structure as favourite).

Read access to the change history of structure forests: each saved forest modification produces a numbered history entry made of add, copy, move and remove changes. Includes a filterable activity query across structures and reconstruction of a forest as it was at an earlier version.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync: Synchronizers: extension modules that keep a structure's forest consistent with some Jira data (links, epics, sprints, filters, and so on). Contains the extension-point interface and a convenience base class, the manager that installs and runs synchronizer instances, the event data handed to incremental runs, and the audit log of actions synchronizers performed.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.uti: Helpers for writing synchronizers: a per-run logger with formatting helpers for issues, rows and forests, a parent lookup that accounts for pending moves, and a change-callback interface.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.template: Extension point for the "create structure" wizard: a template is a module (`new-structure-template` in a plugin descriptor) that contributes a sequence of form steps and then configures the newly created structure (name, permissions, initial content, automation).
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.view: Views: named, shareable grid configurations (columns, display modes, pinned columns) for displaying structures, plus per-structure and global settings saying which views appear in the view menu and which is the default on each page.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.generic: Not part of the public API jar: a service exported by the plugin itself (public OSGi component) that stores the change history of generic items (items managed by the generic item service: each create or update of such an item is recorded with old and new values).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statisti.summary: Callback that contributes named numeric values to the plugin's usage-statistics report. Implemented by plugin components (and potentially other plugins) and registered with `StructureStatisticsRecorder.addStatisticSource`. Marked internal. In the replacement the report is never sent anywhere (SPEC.md §1.8), so sources may be registered but their values are at most kept locally.

members.getStatistics(): Returns a map from statistic name to its current value, computed at the time of the call (for example a count of structures). Called whenever a statistics report is assembled; an exception thrown here is logged and the source is skipped for that report.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.statisti.summary: Service (OSGi component, internal) for recording usage counters. Recording calls are cheap and asynchronous: values are accumulated in memory and periodically (every 10 minutes by default) written to the plugin's local statistics store; data older than 40 days is purged. The original could upload a daily report to the vendor when an administrator opted in; the replacement never uploads usage statistics or contacts the vendor (SPEC.md §1.8). Thread-safe.

members.addUniqueUserCountAsync(String): Records that the current user (as known to `StructureAuth`) used the feature named by the argument; the statistic counts distinct users. Does nothing when there is no current user (anonymous) or when the name is null or blank (a warning is logged). Throws the plugin's stopped exception if the plugin is not running.
members.addTotalCountAsync(String): Increments the total counter named by the argument by 1. Same as `addTotalCountAsync(name, 1.0)`.
members.addTotalCountAsync(String, double): Adds the second argument to the running total of the counter named by the first argument. A null or blank name is ignored with a logged warning. Throws the plugin's stopped exception if the plugin is not running.
members.addToIntValueDistrAsync(String, int, int: Records one observation of an integer value into a histogram. Arguments: statistic prefix, the value, and ascending bin upper bounds. The value falls into the first bin whose bound is greater than or equal to it, or into an overflow bin named `inf` when it exceeds all bounds; the counter `<prefix>.<bound>` (or `<prefix>.inf`) is then incremented by 1. With no bins nothing is recorded.
members.addStatisticSource(com.almworks.jira.str: Registers a source whose values are added to every statistics report assembled afterwards. The same object may be added more than once (it is then queried more than once). Not persisted across restarts.
Unregisters one registration of the given source; does nothing if it was not registered.
members.addTotalCountAndActiveUserAsync(String): Convenience: increments the total counter named by the argument by 1 and also records the current user under the distinct-user statistic `activeUser.<name>`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: A structure's metadata as a mutable, unsaved working copy. Instances are obtained from `StructureManager` (`getStructure`, `getAllStructures`, `createStructure`, copies) and are snapshots: they do not reflect later changes by others. Setters only change the local copy and return the same object for chaining; nothing is persisted until `saveChanges()`. The forest (the rows) is not part of this object; it is accessed via the forest service. Not thread-safe; use one instance per thread.

members.getId(): The structure's numeric ID (positive). For a new structure that has not been saved yet, returns 0.
members.getName(): The structure's name; never null (empty string when unset).
members.getDescription(): The structure's description; never null (empty string when unset).
members.getOwner(): The owner resolved to a Jira user from `getOwnerUserKey()`; null when there is no owner or the user key no longer resolves to a user.
members.getOwnerUserKey(): The Jira user key of the structure's owner, or null when the structure has no owner. The owner can always administer the structure.
members.getPermissions(): A copy of the structure's own permission rules, in evaluation order (later rules override earlier ones for the same user). Never null; changing the returned list does not affect the structure. These rules complement the owner and global administrators, who always have full access.
members.isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission(): True when editing the structure additionally requires that the user can edit the parent issue of any issue being added, moved or removed under it (the parent-issue edit check is applied on every forest change).
members.isArchived(): True when the structure is archived. Archived structures are read-only (forest changes are refused) and are excluded from most listings by default.
members.setName(String): Sets the name in the working copy. Null becomes the empty string; names longer than 190 characters are shortened with a trailing ellipsis. A blank name makes `saveChanges()` fail. Returns this.
members.setDescription(String): Sets the description in the working copy (null clears it). Returns this.
members.setOwner(com.atlassian.jira.user.Applica: Sets the owner in the working copy from a Jira user (null clears the owner); equivalent to `setOwnerUserKey` with the user's key. Returns this.
members.setOwnerUserKey(String): Sets the owner by Jira user key in the working copy; null clears the owner. The key is not validated here; ownership-change permission is checked by `saveChanges()`. Returns this.
members.setPermissions(java.util.Collection): Replaces the permission rules in the working copy with the given rules (null means no rules). Rules are validated on `saveChanges()`. Returns this.
members.setEditRequiresParentIssuePermission(boo: Sets the parent-issue edit check flag (see `isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission`) in the working copy. Returns this.
members.setArchived(boolean): Sets the archived flag in the working copy. Returns this.
members.saveChanges(): Persists the working copy and returns this. If nothing was changed since the copy was obtained or last saved, does nothing. For a new structure, creates it (the ID becomes available from `getId()`), gives it an empty forest and, when no owner was set, makes the current user the owner. Throws `IllegalStateException` when the name is blank. Unless security is overridden (`StructureAuth.sudo`), creation requires the global right to create structures (`StructureException` with `NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE`), and updating requires ADMIN level on the structure (`STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the user has no access at all, `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` otherwise). Changed permission rules are validated (`StructureException` on invalid rules). Assigning the owner to another user requires being a Jira administrator, or holding the Jira user-picker permission together with ADMIN on the structure or being the previous owner; otherwise `STRUCTURE_OWNER_EDIT_DENIED`. Also fails when the plugin license does not allow writes.
members.getEffectivePermission(): The access level the current user has to this structure, computed now from the stored (not the unsaved) settings. `ADMIN` when security is overridden; `NONE` for a structure that has not been saved yet.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Extension point notified after structure forests change. Register with `StructureManager.addListener`. Called synchronously on the thread that finished writing history, once per batch of recorded changes; exceptions are logged and do not affect other listeners. Implementations should be fast and must not assume a particular user context.

members.onStructuresChanged(com.almworks.integer: Called with a map from structure ID to the history entry that was just recorded for that structure (one entry per changed structure in the batch). The map should be treated as read-only.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Main service (OSGi component) for structure metadata: lookup, access checks, creation, copying, deletion and change listeners. Implemented by the plugin. Unless stated otherwise, calls act as the current user from `StructureAuth`, and permission checks are skipped when security is overridden. Methods taking a `PermissionLevel` treat null as "no minimum level", so a null level returns structures even when the user's level is NONE. If the plugin is not available to the current user (license or global access restriction), listings are empty. Lists of structures are sorted by name with the current user's locale collation unless noted. Thread-safe.

members.getStructure(Long, com.almworks.jira.str: Returns the structure with the given ID (first argument) if the current user has at least the given level (second argument; null means any). Throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the ID is null, the structure does not exist or the level is insufficient (the two cases are deliberately indistinguishable). Archived structures are returned too.
members.getAllStructures(com.almworks.jira.struc: All non-archived structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any). Same as `getAllStructures(level, false)`.
All structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any); the second argument includes archived structures when true. Sorted by name. Never null.
Only the archived structures on which the current user has at least the given level (null means any), sorted by name.
Non-archived structures whose owner is the given user and which the current user can at least view, sorted by name. Null user yields an empty list.
members.getStructuresByName(String, com.almworks: Non-archived structures with the given name that the current user can access at the given level. Same as the three-argument form with `false`.

Structures whose name equals the given name ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, accessible at the given level (null means any); the third argument also searches archived structures. A null or blank name returns an empty list. Several structures may share a name.
members.hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser(): True if the current user can view at least one non-archived structure.
members.getSingleViewableStructureId(): If the current user can view exactly one non-archived structure, its ID; otherwise (none, or more than one, or the plugin is not available to the user) null. Used to skip a structure picker. The result may be cached per user.
members.isIssueInStructureNoAccessCheck(Long, Lo: True if the issue (first argument, issue ID) appears in the stored forest of the structure (second argument) according to the plugin's issue-to-structure index. No permission check is made. Only static content counts: issues added by generators are not indexed.
members.getViewableStructuresWithIssue(Long): Non-archived structures the current user can view whose stored forest contains the given issue (by issue ID), sorted the same way as the plugin's structure pickers for the current user. Null issue ID returns an empty list.
members.getStructurePermission(Long): The current user's access level to the structure with the given ID. Returns `PermissionLevel.NONE` when the ID is null or the structure does not exist. Does not take security override into account.
members.getStructurePermission(Long, com.atlassi: The access level of the given user (second argument; null means anonymous) to the given structure. `NONE` when the structure does not exist.
members.isAccessible(Long, com.almworks.jira.str: True when the structure exists and the current user has at least the given level (null level means any existing structure). Always true for an existing structure when security is overridden.
members.isGeneratorConfigurationAllowed(Long, co: True when the given user has at least AUTOMATE level on the structure and also holds the plugin's application permission to configure generators.
members.isEffectorConfigurationAllowed(Long, com: True when the given user has at least AUTOMATE level on the structure and also holds the plugin's application permission to configure effectors.
members.isEffectorExecutionAllowed(Long, com.atl: True when the given user can at least VIEW the structure and also holds the plugin's application permission to run effectors.
members.createStructure(): Returns a new, unsaved `Structure` with no ID, empty name and default settings. Nothing is stored until `saveChanges()` is called on it; set a name first.
members.copyStructure(Long, com.atlassian.jira.u: Creates and saves a copy of the structure (first argument) including its forest, and returns the saved copy. The forest is copied as static content (automation rows are copied as they are). Second argument: owner of the copy, null keeps the source's owner. Third argument: also copy permission rules and the parent-issue flag. The copy's name is a localized "copy of <name>" text including the date. Requires the right to create structures, VIEW on the source, and ADMIN on the source when copying permissions (`StructureException` with the matching error otherwise). The original also fails when its licence is read-only; the replacement is always licensed (SPEC.md §1.1), so this never happens.
members.copyStructureWithoutForest(Long, com.atl: Like `copyStructure` but returns an unsaved copy of the metadata only; the caller must call `saveChanges()`, and the new structure's forest will be empty. Arguments and permission checks are the same.
members.deleteStructure(Long): Deletes the structure, its forest, its change history and its issue index entries, then publishes a structure-deleted event. Null ID does nothing. Requires ADMIN on the structure unless security is overridden (`StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED`, also when the structure does not exist). The original also fails when its licence is read-only, which never happens in the always-licensed replacement. Favourites and views referring to it are not removed here.
Registers a listener for forest changes (see `StructureListener`). Listeners are held strongly until removed; remove them when your plugin stops.
members.removeListener(com.almworks.jira.structu: Unregisters a listener previously added; does nothing if it was not registered.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Service (OSGi component) that stores which structures each user marked as favourite and derives each structure's popularity (number of users who marked it). Implemented by the plugin; values are cached. Thread-safe.

members.isFavorite(Long, com.atlassian.jira.user: True if the given user (second argument) has the structure (first argument) among favourites. False when either argument is null. No access check.
members.setFavorite(Long, com.atlassian.jira.use: Marks (third argument true) or unmarks (false) the structure as a favourite of the given user. Idempotent. Does nothing when the structure ID or user is null. No permission or existence check is made: any structure ID can be stored.
members.getPopularity(Long): Number of users who have the structure as a favourite (0 or more). 0 for a null ID or on storage errors.
members.getFavorites(com.atlassian.jira.user.App: The user's non-archived favourite structures. Same as `getFavorites(user, false)`.

The given user's favourite structures that still exist and that the current user (from `StructureAuth`, not necessarily the given user) can view; the second argument includes archived ones. Sorted as in the plugin's structure pickers for the given user. Null user returns an empty list.
members.getAllFavorites(): A snapshot of all favourites: user key to the ascending list of distinct favourite structure IDs. Users are ordered by key. Includes IDs of structures that may no longer exist. No access check.
members.sortByPopularity(java.util.List, com.atl: Sorts the given mutable list in place: most popular first, ties broken by the plugin's structure ordering for the given user; null elements go last. Null or empty list is left alone.
members.filterByPopularity(java.util.List, int,: Returns a new list with the structures from the first argument whose popularity is within the inclusive range given by the second (minimum) and third (maximum) arguments, preserving order. Null list returns an empty list.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Immutable value: the complete forest of a structure at one version together with the history entry that produced that version. Returned by `HistoryService.getForestVersion`. Public fields only.

members.fullForest: The entire forest of the structure as it was right after the version was recorded.
members.entry: The history entry for this version. For version 0 (the initial empty state) a synthetic entry with no changes, timestamp 0 and no user.
members.weight: Estimated memory size of this object, used by caches. Computed in the constructor from the sizes of the full forest and of every change's forest and row lists; a rough approximation, not a byte count.
members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.f: Creates the value from the full forest (first argument) and its entry (second, must not be null) and computes `weight`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Callback receiving history entries one at a time from `HistoryService`. Implemented by callers, typically as a lambda.

Receives the next entry. Return true to continue, false to stop the iteration early.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Immutable record of one saved modification of a structure's forest, identified by structure ID and version number. Versions of one structure increase by one with every recorded change; each entry lists the elementary changes in the order applied. Created by the plugin when recording history; can be constructed by callers (for example in tests). Equality is by value of all fields.

members.<init>(long, int, int, long, String, Lon: Arguments in order: structure ID, version, previous version, timestamp (milliseconds since epoch), author user key (null or empty string are stored as null), synchronizer instance ID that made the change (null if none), and the list of changes (not copied; must not be null).
members.getStructure(): ID of the structure the entry belongs to.
members.getVersion(): Forest version produced by this entry (1 for the first recorded change).
members.getPrevVersion(): Forest version that this entry was applied to. Normally `getVersion() - 1`.
members.getTimestamp(): When the change was recorded, in milliseconds since the epoch.
members.getUserKey(): Jira user key of the user who made the change; null when unknown or anonymous.
members.getSynchronizer(): ID of the synchronizer instance that made the change, or null if it was not made by a synchronizer.
members.getChanges(): The changes in this entry, in the order applied. Never null. Entries returned by `getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges` have an empty list. In activity queries the list may be shortened (changes involving rows the user cannot see are filtered out) or truncated by a change limit.
members.toString(): Debug text listing all fields; format not part of the contract.
members.equals(Object): True for another `HistoryEntry` with equal structure, versions, timestamp, user key, synchronizer and change list.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Immutable description of one elementary forest change inside a `HistoryEntry`: which rows were added, copied, moved or removed, and where. Positions are given as a parent path (list of row IDs from a root down to the parent, empty or null for top level) plus the preceding sibling. Equality is by value.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.s: Arguments in order: operation; the forest fragment affected; path from (old parent path); after from (old preceding sibling); path to (new parent path); after to (new preceding sibling); direction; original rows. Values are stored as given (not copied).
members.getForest(): The forest fragment that was added, copied (the new rows), moved or removed, with its subtrees.
members.getPathFrom(): For MOVE and REMOVE: the row IDs from the top level down to the former parent of the fragment (empty when it was at top level). Null for ADD and COPY.
members.getAfterFrom(): For MOVE and REMOVE: the former preceding sibling, as a list of at most one row ID (empty when the fragment was first among its siblings). Null for ADD and COPY. During forest reconstruction the plugin may prepend further preceding siblings to this list.
members.getPathTo(): For ADD, COPY and MOVE: the row IDs from the top level down to the new parent, including the parent itself (empty for top level). Null for REMOVE.
members.getAfterTo(): For ADD, COPY and MOVE: the new preceding sibling as a list of at most one row ID (empty when inserted first). Null for REMOVE.
members.getDirection(): For MOVE: 1 if the fragment moved further down the forest, -1 if it moved up, 0 if its position index did not change. 0 for other operations.
members.getOriginalRows(): For COPY: for each row of `getForest()` in the same order, the ID of the row it was copied from, or 0 when that source row was not (or no longer) in this structure. Null for other operations.
members.toString(): Debug text listing all fields; format not part of the contract.
members.equals(Object): True for another `Change` with equal operation, forest, paths, preceding siblings, direction and original rows.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Kind of an elementary forest change recorded in history. Each constant has a lower-case external name used in REST and query parameters.

members.ADD: Rows were inserted into the forest (external name `add`).
members.COPY: Rows were inserted as copies of other rows (external name `copy`).
members.MOVE: Existing rows were moved to another position (external name `move`).
members.REMOVE: Rows were removed from the forest (external name `remove`).
members.forExternalName(String): The constant whose external name equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive); null when there is no match or the argument is null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Immutable filter for `HistoryService.queryActivity`. All conditions are combined with AND. Each dimension has an inclusion (`is...`) and an exclusion (`not...`) list; for structures, authors, issues and projects only the inclusion list is applied when it is non-empty, otherwise the exclusion list. ID lists must be sorted ascending. Created by its constructors; all collections are copied or defaulted to empty, never null (except `operations`).

members.ALL_OPERATIONS: Unmodifiable list of all `Operation` constants in declaration order.
members.operations: Operations to match: an entry matches when it contains at least one change of these kinds. Null means all operations (no restriction); the constructor stores null when all four were given.
members.isIssuesSorted: Issue IDs (sorted): match entries that touched at least one of these issues. Never null.
members.notIssuesSorted: Issue IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, match entries that touched some issue other than these. Never null.
members.isStructuresSorted: Structure IDs (sorted): match entries of any of these structures. Never null.
members.notStructuresSorted: Structure IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, exclude entries of these structures. Never null.
members.isAuthors: User keys: match entries made by one of these users. A null element in the authors argument makes the constructor throw `NullPointerException`. Never null.
members.notAuthors: User keys: when there is no inclusion set, exclude entries made by these users. Never null.
members.isProjectsSorted: Project IDs (sorted): match entries that touched issues of at least one of these projects. Never null.
members.notProjectsSorted: Project IDs (sorted): when there is no inclusion list, match entries touching issues of some other project. Never null.
members.isSynchronizersSorted: Synchronizer instance IDs (sorted) to include. Special values: -2 means "made without a synchronizer", -1 means "made by any synchronizer". Never null.
members.notSynchronizersSorted: Synchronizer instance IDs (sorted) to exclude, with the same special values -2 and -1. Applied together with the inclusion list. Never null.
members.isAncestors: Item identities: keep only entries having a change located under one of these items (an item on the from or to parent path), or, when an issue or project filter is set, a change whose fragment contains such an item with a matching issue below it. Never null.
members.notAncestors: Item identities: drop entries whose every change is located under one of these items, in the same sense as `isAncestors`. Never null.
members.minDate: Earliest timestamp to include (inclusive), milliseconds since epoch; null for no lower bound.
members.maxDate: Latest timestamp to include (inclusive), milliseconds since epoch; null for no upper bound.
members.startId: Paging cursor: only entries whose internal history key is strictly less than this value are returned. The key of an entry is `(structureId << 32) | version`. Null to start from the newest.
members.<init>(Iterable, com.almworks.integers.L: Arguments in field order: operations, issues in, issues out, structures in, structures out, authors in, authors out, projects in, projects out, synchronizers in, synchronizers out, ancestors in, ancestors out, min date, max date, start key. Any argument may be null (meaning no restriction). For operations pass `ALL_OPERATIONS` (or any collection containing all four) for no restriction. Not determined: what a null or empty operations argument does in a query; the original stores an empty set and then builds no operation condition for it, so behaviour is undefined; a replacement should treat it as no restriction or reject it. Long lists are kept as given (not copied) and must already be sorted; dates are converted to milliseconds.
members.<init>(long, Long): Query for all activity of one structure (first argument), all operations, starting below the given paging key (second argument, nullable).
members.toString(): Compact debug text listing the non-empty conditions; computed once and cached. Format not part of the contract.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Service (OSGi component) for reading recorded forest history. Implemented by the plugin. Only `queryActivity` and `getForestVersion` apply the current user's permissions; the per-structure methods read history without access checks, so callers must check access themselves. Thread-safe.

members.queryActivity(com.almworks.jira.structur: Streams entries matching the query (first argument) to the consumer (third), newest first (by timestamp, then key, descending), with all their changes. Second argument: maximum number of entries delivered (0 or less for no limit). Unless security is overridden, entries of structures the current user cannot view are skipped, and changes are filtered by row visibility only loosely: a change is removed when the user can see none of its rows, but rows the user cannot see may still appear in a kept change (as ancestors in its path, or in its after-lists). An entry with no changes is never delivered, whether or not anything was filtered. Stops when the consumer returns false.

Same as the three-argument form, but the third argument limits how many changes are loaded per entry (0 or less loads all); the consumer receives each entry together with its total number of changes, which may exceed the size of the truncated change list; this total is counted before visibility filtering.
members.getHistoryEntries(long, int, int, com.al: Streams the entries of the structure (first argument) with versions greater than the second argument and up to and including the third, oldest first, with changes. A negative "from" version means from the very beginning. Returns nothing when both versions are equal. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when "to" is less than "from" or negative. No access check.
members.getHistoryEntries(long, int, int): Same range and rules as the streaming form, collected into a list (oldest first).
members.getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges(long, in: Same as `getHistoryEntries(long, int, int)` but each entry's change list is empty (cheaper when only metadata is needed).
members.getLatestHistoryEntryVersion(long): Highest recorded history version of the structure, or 0 when it has no history. No access check.
members.getEarliestHistoryEntryVersionGtEqDate(l: Lowest version of the structure (first argument) whose entry was recorded at or after the timestamp (second argument, epoch milliseconds); 0 when there is none.
members.getEntryCount(long): Number of history entries stored for the structure.
members.getEntryCountGtEqDate(long, long): Number of history entries of the structure (first argument) recorded at or after the timestamp (second argument, epoch milliseconds).
members.getForestVersion(long, int): Reconstructs the full forest of the structure (first argument) as of the given version (second argument) and returns it with that version's entry. Version 0 gives the initial state with a synthetic empty entry. Requires VIEW access for the current user; otherwise `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. A version above the current version, or missing from history, gives `StructureException` `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. A version below 0 is checked only by an assertion: with assertions enabled (as tests run) it throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the result is not specified. Results are cached; the forest is not filtered by row visibility.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.structur.summary: Callback for `HistoryService.queryActivity` with a per-entry change limit. Implemented by callers.

Receives the next entry (first argument) and the total number of changes the entry has (second argument), which may be larger than the possibly truncated change list. Return true to continue, false to stop.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.sync.Abs.summary: Recommended base class for synchronizer extension modules (`structure-synchronizer` module type in a plugin descriptor). Supplies JSON-map parameter storage, issue lookup helpers, descriptor access, and audit logging: subclasses implement `doSync` and `doResync`, returning a result whose actions are written to the `SyncAuditLog`. Instances are created by the plugin framework (one per module) and shared by all sync instances of that module, so they must be thread-safe and keep per-instance state in `SyncInstance.transientData`. Subclasses still implement `isAvailable`, `isAutosyncSupported`, the description and form methods.

members.myStructureComponents: The service bundle passed to the constructor, for subclass use.
members.myStructureManager: The structure manager taken from the service bundle.
members.myRowManager: The row manager taken from the service bundle.
members.myAuditLog: The synchronizer audit log taken from the service bundle; used by `sync` and `resync` to record actions.
members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.S: Creates the synchronizer, taking the audit log, structure manager and row manager from the given service bundle (normally injected).
members.init(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.syn: Stores the module descriptor returned later by `getDescriptor()`. Expected to be called once, before use, with this module's descriptor by the module-descriptor framework. Not determined: the plugin's own code never calls it; the call comes from the platform's module initialisation.
